one_month_reasoning: Inside the window: Q3 2026 results on Oct 29 with the rolled-forward 2027-2031 capital, financing and EPS plan (source 25): a larger plan (the deck already shows $70B+ including $10B+ line of sight, source 27) lifts rate-base growth but carries ~40% equity on the increment, and the NSPM 2027-28 base-rate freeze (source 6) may weigh on the 2027 starting point, so the event is two-sided. Also the MPUC's action on the AG/CUB reconsideration petitions (the Oct 19 deadline passed; I found no reported outcome, source 11), the MPUC's NSPM gas decision expected in November (source 27), and the 10-yr after a September Fed hike to a 4% upper bound with utilities 'most oversold since 2023' (XLU -6% in a month, source 30); oversold readings argue mildly for short-term reversal, rate momentum against. An Anthropic IPO roadshow, if it starts in the window, draws AI and mega-cap money first; XEL's holders are mostly income and utility funds. No strong edge: a near-symmetric lognormal around $77.0 (spot plus a small reversal tilt), monthly vol ~5.4% (19%/3.5), with a 10% weight on a 10% vol component for the Oct-29 plan event.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount has persisted since the 2024 Smokehouse Creek fire and is structural through the horizon: (1) wildfire liability with no Colorado shield (the 2025 liability plan was dropped, source 32; draft Bill 5 only) and an open Texas AG suit with ~$80M of Smokehouse insurance left (source 2); (2) Moody's negative outlook and the heaviest equity programme in the group ($7B base plan, 69.7M forward shares, 40% equity on any incremental capex, source 27); (3) lag: PSCo earns 7.22% vs 9.3% allowed on a 13-month historical test year, and NSPM proposes a 2027-28 base-rate freeze (sources 5, 6, 27). Offsetting: my 2026-28 EPS CAGR of 8.3% (inside the company's 6-8+% objective, not the '9%+' I cited in round 1) is at or above the 7.8% peer median, and the first 3 GW of data-center load is contracted under tariffs with minimum bills, so I hold the discount rather than widen it.

thesis_break_reason: $63 is ~18% below today, ~8% under the $68.72 52-week low (set with the 10-yr near its October high), 13.3x my horizon NTM EPS ($4.74) and 14.1x today's NTM consensus ($4.456), below every regulated peer but ES. Rates alone did not take it there, so a close below $63 most likely means a fundamental break: a new utility-ignited wildfire with liability beyond insurance, a Texas AG outcome that blocks recovery, regulators forcing earned ROE toward 8% (MN freeze approved with no offset, PSCo lag widening), a rejected Google ESA plus a capital-plan cut, or a downgrade that forces block equity. Re-underwrite rather than average down.

reverse_dcf_check: Engine: the P/E leg ($81.4) implies a WACC of 5.7% with 3.5% terminal growth on my 2026-30 driver path; my CAPM WACC of 5.97% gives $62.6. Put differently, 17.2x NTM EPS implies ~8% EPS growth through 2030 (rate base ~11% less dilution and lag) and ~3.5% after, with earned ROE held ~8.7-9%, and an EV of ~1.37x the horizon rate base vs ~1.15x steady-state economics at my WACC. Plausible because the first 3 GW of data-center generation is in the base plan under minimum-bill tariffs and allowed ROEs are 9.2-9.6%, but only if those ROEs hold and equity stays near 40% of incremental capex. The probability-weighted long-dated risks sum to ~-$8.3/sh, roughly the 1.65-turn discount to the peer median (1.65 x $4.74 = $7.8), so they are carried in the multiple, the terminal growth and the bear scenario.

reasoning: Round 2 changes: (1) shares: the 10-Q shows only the 2025 forwards (27.3M) settle before the horizon, so horizon shares are 662M, not 690M, and FY2027/28 averages ~652M/693M; (2) with the right share count, my round-1 ROE assumption would have put FY2027 EPS near $4.69, well above consensus ($4.54) and the company's 6-8+% EPS growth objective in the Q2 2026 deck (I wrongly cited '9%+' in round 1), so I re-derived the effective ROE at 8.70% for 2027-28 (PSCo 7.22% TTM on a historical test year, NSPM freeze) and rebuilt the EPS path: $4.49 / $4.81, NTM $4.74; (3) P/E 17.2x, XEL's current 0.91x of the 18.85x median on the same NTM basis (round 1 compared against an FY2027 multiple); (4) DCF: terminal growth 3.5% with capex normalised consistently (round 1 reinvested for 4.3% growth while growing 4%), WACC 5.97% on 2026 issuance coupons, net debt $49.4B with only $2B of forward proceeds before the horizon: DCF $62.6 (23% below the P/E leg, explained in dcf_check). Engine fair value $77.65 (P/E leg $81.4 x 0.8 + DCF $62.6 x 0.2). Industry read: data-center demand: ~2 GW contracted, ~4 GW more targeted by YE2027, Google (Pine Island ESA; Abernathy backstop in SPS) is the main counterparty and is also Anthropic's largest compute partner per the WSJ's S-1 report, so the S-1 is an indirect demand positive; no verified Anthropic site in Xcel territory (TeraWulf filing names Fluidstack/Google at Abernathy; Anthropic's Texas sites are in Central Texas). Backlash: the S-1's risk factor matches what is visible in MN (AG opposes the Google ESA as filed; moratorium push). Counterparty risk sits mainly with large-load tariff terms (MN approved; CO pending; SPS TX/NM not yet filed, the gap). Macro: the Fed raised its upper bound to 4% in September and utilities sold off (XLU -6% in a month); the 10-yr, not IPO flows, explains XEL's -5.5% year. IPO liquidity question: XEL's holders are income/utility funds with little overlap with IPO buyers; a flow-driven dip toward $70 (15.7x today's NTM consensus, 14.8x my horizon EPS) without a change in rate-base EPS, the 10-yr or regulatory facts would be a buying opportunity; below $63 (thesis break) re-check wildfire and regulatory news first; the Oct-29 equity plan is the nearer risk. Ladder: bear $64.8 (25%, incl. a 3% wildfire tail at $52), base $78.5 (50%), bull $91 (25%), within-scenario vol ~11%: median ~$78.3, log-sd ~17%, below the 19% realised vol because regulated EPS is visible. Research limits: no outcome found yet for the MN reconsideration or the CO large-load tariff; no 2027 Colorado liability bill found.

model_inputs.structure_note: Regulated utility. Value carried by a P/E leg (w 0.8) on a rate-base EPS build (avg rate base x 53.7% blended authorised equity ratio x effective earned ROE incl. AFUDC-equity, less after-tax HoldCo interest, over the 10-Q forward-settlement share path), and a driver DCF (w 0.2: forward P/E 76.68/4.54 = 16.9x sits in the 15.0-19.6x band). years margins are set from the build: EBIT = NI/(1-tax) + net interest, so implied EPS matches the build (FY2027 (4,727-1,940)x1.05/652 = $4.49; FY2028 (5,543-2,310)x1.03/693 = $4.81). Capex includes AFUDC so FCF is consistent; FY2030 capex is normalised to D&A + 3.5% rate-base growth to match the 3.5% Gordon terminal. Probability-weighted Texas AG / Smokehouse claim as an adjustment.
model_inputs.gap_note: fair_value.value = engine base horizon value (77.65). My 12-month ladder is centred slightly higher (median ~$78.3) and its bear is milder than the engine's ($64.8 vs $60.7) because over 12 months the price follows the group P/E and today's price; the engine's bear is dragged by the DCF leg, which loses ~$20/sh for +40bp of WACC.

model_inputs.dcf_check: DCF $62.6 is 23% below the P/E leg ($81.4). (1) Discount rate: my CAPM WACC is 5.97%; the engine's reverse DCF says the P/E leg implies 5.7%. With WACC - g only ~2.5 points, every 25bp moves the DCF ~$15/sh (6.22% -> $48.2; 5.72% -> $80.2), so the gap is within the CAPM's own error band (beta 0.40 vs 0.45, ERP 4.5% vs 5%). (2) Economics: after-tax return on rate base ~6.35% (53.7% x ~8.7% ROE + 46.3% x ~4.5% x 0.79) vs 5.97% WACC gives a steady-state EV of ~(6.35-3.5)/(5.97-3.5) = 1.15x rate base; the P/E leg implies ~1.37x horizon rate base, i.e. the market capitalises the ROE-over-CoE spread at a lower rate. (3) Round 1's -39% gap was partly my own inconsistency: terminal capex at 42% of revenue reinvested for ~4.3% rate-base growth while the Gordon growth was 4.0%, so the terminal ROIC on new capital was below WACC. The gap is sector-wide (peers at 18.85x would show it too), so the DCF keeps its table weight as an anchor and the P/E is not moved toward it.
